A typical caller consuming `entries_prefixed` output directly gets **silently wrong results** — foreign records presented as members of the queried collection, no error anywhere. That's a stronger reason to file upstream promptly than our own 500s were.

question from the implementation

Pick **option 2 (errors counter)** — and I'd push back on the implementer's recommended option 1, because it subtly breaks the doctrine it claims to reuse.

The crate's "staleness is the alarm" convention distinguishes two states: a **whole-pass failure** (couldn't list candidates, couldn't list expired owners → early return, timestamp untouched) versus a **completed pass with partial errors** (per-account skip, counted in `stats.errors`). The existing sweeps freeze the timestamp only for the first. Option 1 as worded — freeze on any `errors > 0` — merges the two, and our own incident shows why that's wrong: your account's reconcile failed on *every* pass for 6 hours, and with MM-473 unfixed it would fail for days or weeks. Under option 1, one chronically broken account makes `blob_gc_last_run_timestamp` **permanently** stale. The staleness alarm becomes a constant condition the operator learns to ignore — which destroys its value as the acute "GC is wedged" signal, for exactly the sweep where wedging matters most. Chronic alarms are worse than no alarms; they take the working doctrine down with them.

The counter keeps each signal meaning one thing: timestamp = "the pass runs to completion," `errors > 0` = "it's skipping someone — go find out who." That's alertable without ambiguity, and post-MM-472 the skipped state is exactly what an operator needs to notice, since a skipped account is now silently leaking disk instead of silently losing data.

Two supporting points for the implementing session:

- **This isn't scope creep — it's a transfer from MM-474.** Item 2 of MM-474 ("make `errors > 0` distinguishable in sweep_status/metrics, per-sweep errors counter") is *exactly* this, and I flagged it there as the highest-value item. Pulling it into the MM-472 PR is right because it's the operator-facing half of the same fix: the code change converts deletion into a leak, the counter is what makes the leak visible. If they take option 2, they should drop a comment on MM-474 noting item 2 shipped with MM-472 so the next session doesn't re-implement it. The rest of MM-474 (physical-vs-owned divergence, `didWebHosting`) stays put.
- **Keep the existing whole-pass freezes unchanged.** The early-return paths should still leave the timestamp stale — that acute signal stays intact, which is also the answer to option 3: "both" isn't louder, it's the same conflation as option 1 plus a counter.

Option 4 is defensible if they want the minimal reviewable diff — the deletion risk is gone either way — but the counter is one instrument, one `sweep_status` field, one `/v1/admin/health` line, and one AGENTS.md table row. Small enough to belong with the fix whose consequences it reports.

Silent, irreversible data loss — confirmed in production on 2026-07-25.

## The bug

`run_blob_gc`'s sweep phase was not gated on whether an account's reconcile succeeded in the same pass.

Reconcile is the *only* thing that clears the `temp_until` grace clock `uploadBlob` stamps on every new `blob_owners` row. When `reconcile_account` errors it propagates with `?` before either the pin loop or the release loop runs, so nothing is pinned permanent. Phase 2 then calls `list_expired_temp_owners`, which scans **all** accounts with no reference to which ones reconciled — so once the grace expired it deleted the ownership row, the physical `blobs` row, and the file. `blob_mirror` faithfully propagated the row deletions to the bucket, destroying the off-volume copy too.

The failure is indistinguishable from success at the sweep's vantage point: "this account references nothing" and "we could not compute what this account references" both look like an unpinned row.

`did:web:malpercio.dev` lost **534 blobs** this way. `errors=1` was present on every pass for ~6 hours beforehand and each one still logged `"blob GC pass complete"`. Recovery was only possible because the wallet's iCloud media backup existed.

## The fix

Collect the DIDs whose reconcile errored this pass and exclude them from the sweep. **Fail closed** — an account whose live references we could not compute must never have its blobs collected. It then leaks disk until the underlying fault is fixed, which is strictly the right trade against irreversible deletion.

Skipping per-DID also protects shared bytes for free: `delete_blob_if_unowned` only reclaims when the *last* owner is gone, so a CID a skipped account still owns can never lose its last owner, and no other owner's sweep can reclaim the physical row or file either.

The exclusion is a `HashSet` filter in Rust rather than pushed into the SQL deliberately — binding a variable-length DID list into the query would bury the safety property inside a `WHERE` clause where the next person editing it cannot see why it is there.

## Observability

The ticket's secondary item. A stale timestamp already means *"the sweep is dead"*; it cannot also express *"the sweep ran but left work undone"* — and those call for different operator responses ("go look at the server" vs "go look at that account"). Collapsing them is what made the incident invisible for six hours.

So an errored pass still records (it ran, and it did collect for every healthy account), and the skipped work gets its own channel:

- `blob_gc_errors_total` metric
- an `errors` field on `SweepRun`, surfaced by `GET /v1/admin/health`
- the pass logged at `warn` as *"pass incomplete"* rather than at `info` as *"pass complete"*

`errors` goes on the shared `SweepRun` rather than a blob-GC-specific field because the fault class generalizes — `labeler_watch` and `blob_scrub` both have per-item error paths that vanish into logs today and can adopt it without another schema change.

**Wire compatibility:** the health response gains a field. `HealthSweepRun` in the admin-companion is not `deny_unknown_fields`, so nothing breaks; the console just does not display it yet. Surfacing it there is filed separately and overlaps MM-474.

## Regression test

`gc_skips_sweep_for_an_account_whose_reconcile_failed` — account A's repo walk errors, both A and a healthy B hold an expired unreferenced blob. Asserts A's ownership row, blob row, and file all survive while B's is collected normally.

Verified **both directions**: green as written, and failing with `expired: 2` (both accounts swept) when the exclusion is disabled. That check mattered — my first version of this test was a **false negative** that asserted nothing. I had assumed block storage was DID-scoped and broke A's walk by pointing it at B's root; but `blocks` is a globally content-addressed byte store with only `block_owners` scoped per account, so A read B's block and reconciled successfully. The test now uses a CID stored in `blobs`, which is structurally valid but has no block behind it. The reasoning is in a comment so it is not repeated.

## Note for deploy

The manual `UPDATE blob_owners SET temp_until = NULL WHERE account_did = 'did:web:malpercio.dev'` mitigation is **still load-bearing** and this only supersedes it once deployed.

Separately, this does not address *why* that account's repo walk errors. That account will now leak disk indefinitely instead of losing data — the intended trade — but the root cause is still open and out of scope here. I would keep the manual pin until it is diagnosed.

## Review: PR #437 — Never sweep the blobs of an account whose reconcile failed (MM-472)

### Overview

Implements exactly what MM-472 scoped, plus the errors-counter observability we settled on in the option-2 discussion: a `HashSet` of DIDs whose reconcile errored, checked before each sweep candidate; `blob_gc_errors_total`; `errors` on `SweepRun` → `/v1/admin/health`; pass-level log downgraded from `info "complete"` to `warn "incomplete"` when work was skipped. 199 additions, 7 files, changelog fragments present.

**This is correct and I'd merge it.** I verified the mechanism against the sweep's `WHERE` clause and the incident's failure shape; the exclusion sits at the right point (before `sweep_expired_owner`, so neither the ownership row, the physical row, nor the file can be touched), and the shared-bytes argument in the PR body is sound — a skipped account's surviving row means no CID it owns can lose its *last* owner, so `delete_blob_if_unowned` is inert for other owners too.

### Especially good

- **The test is real.** Verified in both directions per the PR body, and the false-negative catch — breaking A's walk via a `blobs`-stored CID rather than another account's root, because `blocks` is globally content-addressed — is exactly the trap; the comment explaining it will save the next person. All referenced helpers (`get_owner`, `seed_account_with_repo`, `gc_state`, `add_blob`) exist.
- **Doctrine preserved precisely.** Whole-pass early returns still leave the timestamp stale (acute signal), partial errors record with a fresh timestamp + nonzero `errors` (chronic signal). The admin_health doc comment even keeps the route's no-verdicts rule intact.
- **Generalizing `errors` onto shared `SweepRun`** rather than a blob-GC-only field, with `now()` defaulting to 0 so the other five sweeps compile untouched — right call, and it pre-plumbs `labeler_watch`/`blob_scrub` adoption.
- Per-DID skip tally instead of 534 log lines per pass; the rationale comment cites why.

### Findings (all minor)

1. **`blob_gc_errors` isn't exercised in the rendered-names pinning test** ([metrics.rs](crates/pds/src/metrics.rs) `rendered_names_match_prometheus_conventions`). That test exists to catch `_total` suffix drift, and this counter's rendered name is precisely what operators will write alert rules against. One `.add(1, &[])` + one `contains("blob_gc_errors_total")` assertion. The existing test only samples representative instruments, so this is consistent-but-improvable rather than a break.

2. **Doc wording overstates what `errors` counts.** AGENTS.md says "`errors` counts accounts and blobs the pass **skipped**" and the health-field doc says "items that pass skipped." In the code, a skipped account contributes **1** (its reconcile failure) regardless of blob count — the incident account would report `errors: 1`, not 534; per-blob skip counts live only in the warn log. Either tighten the wording ("reconcile failures plus individual sweep errors") or add `skipped` blob counts into the tally — I'd tighten the wording; the account count is the more actionable number anyway.

3. **`stats.errors` mixes two failure kinds** — reconcile failures and `sweep_expired_owner` failures — in one counter. That's fine (both mean "pass left work undone"), but worth one clause in the `names::BLOB_GC_ERRORS` doc so nobody later assumes it's purely the skip count.

### Checked and clean

- No ticket refs in `.rs` or AGENTS.md prose; changelog fragment filenames match the gate's convention.
- Wire compat confirmed (above), and the health-route test covers the new field including the fresh-timestamp-with-errors case.
- No security or performance concerns; the `HashSet` and per-DID map are bounded by candidate count.

`list_records_json` stripped the prefix with `strip_prefix(..).unwrap_or(key)`, so a leaked key survived whole and the re-concatenated MST key (`dev.cocore.compute.paymentAuthorization/garden.goals.profile/self`) resolved to nothing → `NotFound` → 500. ## Review: PR #438 — Bound listRecords to the requested collection's key range (MM-473)

### Overview

Replaces the `strip_prefix(..).unwrap_or(key)` closure with a three-way `classify` — `Take` (prefix stripped), `Skip` (sorts before the range), `Stop` (sorts past it) — applied in both traversal branches, plus two regression tests and a changelog fragment. 135 additions, 2 files.

**Correct, and I'd merge it.** I verified the load-bearing pieces independently:

- **The `Stop` shortcut is sound, not just plausible.** For any key `k > prefix` that doesn't carry the prefix, the first differing byte position falls within `prefix.len()`, and that position decides the comparison against *every* key of the form `prefix + suffix` — so `k` sorts after all possible members and ascending order guarantees nothing further can match. This also correctly handles the `"abc/"` vs `"abc0"` adjacency (`'/'` = 0x2F sorts before `'0'`): a prefix-carrying key can never appear after a `Stop` key.
- **Both branches are covered.** The `reverse` branch materialises the stream in ascending order before reversing, so `break` on `Stop` during collection is equally valid there.
- **Fail-closed is genuinely preserved.** A leaked key now never reaches the resolve loop at all (filtered at classify), and a legitimate member's `full_key = prefix + rkey` reconstructs the original key exactly. The property MM-473 flagged as must-not-lose — never resolving a foreign key verbatim — holds by construction.

### Especially good

- The tests attack the *mechanism* (short keys flanking a long-named collection), not the incident's topology — consistent with the probe finding that key length, not node structure, is the trigger. Sweeping `limit` 1..=8 × both directions × value-identity assertions is exactly the "never a foreign record" guarantee, and the cursor test covers the pagination half.
- The performance framing in the comment is accurate and worth having: a 5-record collection's page previously walked `limit` entries of whatever followed it; now it's bounded by the collection plus pre-range yields.

1. **The two empty-prefix call sites deserve a one-line warning comment.** [list_missing_blobs.rs:153](crates/pds/src/routes/list_missing_blobs.rs:153) and [check_account_status.rs:151](crates/pds/src/routes/check_account_status.rs:151) are safe *only because* `""` degenerates the broken upstream bounds check into a full walk. ## Review: PR #441 — Distinguish blob ownership loss from byte loss (MM-474)

### Overview

Three additive read-side surfaces, no migration: `uploadedBlobCount`/`uploadedBlobBytes` on per-account storage (from `blobs.account_did`, the V039 first-uploader column), `blobUnownedCount`/`blobUnownedBytes` on admin health (physical rows no `blob_owners` row claims), and `didWebHosting` on the account listing. Six tests, spec + AGENTS.md updated. 376 additions, 10 files.

**Correct, and I'd merge after one fix.** Verified independently: the `NOT EXISTS` probe rides `idx_blob_owners_cid` (V039), so no table-scan concern; the admin-companion's health/listing structs are not `deny_unknown_fields` (only `RepoRefSubject` is), so the new fields are wire-safe; `/v1/admin/health` and `/v1/admin/accounts` aren't in provisioning-api-spec.md, so updating only the storage section there is complete, not an omission.

### The design calls are right

- **`uploaded*` over "physical"** — agreed; the column literally records the uploader, and calling it physical would invite reading it as a corrected ownership count, which the doc comments correctly warn against.
- **Both placements** — agreed, and the asymmetry is real: the unowned pair is the *alarm* (baseline ~0 structurally, because `delete_blob_if_unowned` drops row and owner together — no threshold tuning), while the per-account pair is the *diagnostic*. The PR body's observation that the unowned alarm fires without the sweep having stopped is exactly the property the incident lacked.
- The tests hit the precise incident shape — delete ownership rows under a live account, assert the ownership view zeroes while the uploader view holds — plus the benign-sharing direction that keeps the readout from being misread as a fault detector.

### Findings

1. **Bruno response docs are now stale — the repo rule requires updating them** (root AGENTS.md: *"changing any route (…response shape…), update the corresponding `.bru`"*). Three files carry per-field `docs` blocks that no longer match: `account_storage.bru` (missing `uploadedBlobCount`/`uploadedBlobBytes`), `admin_health.bru` (missing `blobUnownedCount`/`blobUnownedBytes`), `admin_list_accounts.bru` (missing `didWebHosting`). `bruno-parity` passed because it checks **paths only** — this is precisely the gap AGENTS.md says the manual rule covers. Only real ask before merge.

2. **One honest-limitation clause worth adding** (nit, doc-comment level): the uploader witness reads 0/0 in the incident's own *end state* too — when blob GC does the destroying, physical rows die with their last owner, so both witnesses zero. What the pair makes HTTP-legible is the *diagnosis*: `owned=0, uploaded>0` → ownership loss; `owned=0, uploaded=0` → bytes gone (the SQL-shell conclusion we drew by hand on 2026-07-25). The current comments describe the first case; one sentence naming the second would stop an operator from reading `uploaded=0` as "nothing was ever here."

3. **Bookkeeping, not this PR:** "Closes MM-474" is right (all three items land: 1 here, 2 via #437's `SweepRun::errors`, 3 here), but #438's outstanding **atrium-repo upstream report** must not be parked on MM-474's checklist or it dies with the close — confirm it has its own ticket.

### Checked and clean

- SQL: user input still bound, never spliced; the new select column follows the `FLAGGED_SQL` derived-bool pattern; `did_web_hosting` isn't part of the sort key or cursor, so pagination is untouched.
- No new routes → no new `.bru` files needed; changelog fragment reads well; no ticket refs in `.rs`/AGENTS.md prose; extra per-request query on an admin-only endpoint is fine.
- The `db/AGENTS.md` `server_stats.rs` row update and the routes-table updates keep the docs honest, including the ~0-baseline reasoning.

**Verdict: approve once the three `.bru` docs blocks are updated (item 1).** Items 2–3 are a nit and a reminder.

Closes [MM-475](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-475/didweb-sovereign-sessions-and-wallet-confirmed-oauth-consent).

## Why

Both passwordless auth paths were hard-gated to `did:plc`, so a `did:web` account carrying no password had no way to authenticate at all — and every wallet-migrated account is passwordless, since the migration `createAccount` request has no `password` field and the server stores NULL by design.

That is more than a login inconvenience. `SessionProvider::full_access_client` is the seam every authenticated wallet operation on a Custos-hosted identity goes through, and its ladder ends at `NeedsUnlock` → biometric sovereign login. `restore_blob_backup` sits on that seam. So for a passwordless `did:web`, **the wallet's own iCloud media restore was reachable only while the refresh chain from migration survived** — once it lapsed, sovereign login 401'd on the `is_plc_did` gate and the recovery path was gone. This was on the critical path during the MM-472 recovery.

## The change is one lookup

Signature verification was already method-agnostic (`crypto::verify_did_key_signature` over a `did:key:` URI, P-256 and secp256k1). The only PLC-specific step was the authority lookup, and the `did:web` counterpart primitive already existed.

New `crates/pds/src/identity/authority.rs` exposes `authorized_signing_keys(state, did)`, dispatching `did:plc` → the existing `fetch_current_plc_state` path, `did:web` → `resolve_web_did_document` plus the policy below. It lives in `identity/` because routes may not import one another — the `is_plc_did` gate was duplicated verbatim in both route files, which is the symptom of the missing abstraction. Both routes now delete their copy and share the lookup. Their existing `rejected()` / `approval_rejected()` helpers already collapse every failure to one opaque message, so no new enumeration surface appears. The wallet side needed nothing: `sovereign_login_impl` never inspected the DID method.

## Policy

**Authority is exactly `{did}#device`, and nothing else.** Not "any verificationMethod": `#atproto`'s private key is Custos-held, so a broader set would let this server sign its own sovereign-session envelope for an account it hosts. `create_did.rs` already enforces `#device` specifically when promoting a new `did:web`, so this keeps one rule across both paths. The predicate matches that one (`type == "Multikey"`, `controller == did`, exact `{did}#device` id), differing only in shape — promotion *verifies* a known key by comparing `publicKeyMultibase`, this *discovers* it by extracting that field, rendered `did:key:{multibase}` since a PLC rotation set stores URIs. A document with multiple `#device`-shaped entries is malformed (duplicate `id` already violates DID Core) and fails closed rather than resolving by array order. Resolution is live; the `did_documents` cache is never consulted, because `POST /v1/did-web/document` can write it.

**Gated to self-hosted, server-side.** That same route lets an account rewrite its served document under mere session auth, so on a Custos-hosted `did:web` a stolen session could install an attacker `#device` key and bootstrap sovereign sessions — privilege escalation with no key compromise. `did:plc` has no equivalent hole: rewriting a rotation set needs an existing rotation key, and plc.directory is external.

The gate is **exact rather than approximate**: `POST /v1/did-web/document` already refuses unless hosting is enabled, so `did_web_hosting_enabled_at IS NULL` *is* the condition "no session-authed rewrite is possible", with no gap in either direction. Enforcement is in the lookup, not the client — the route stays live for other clients and for accounts that already opted in.

Making `#device` immutable across such an edit would let the gate be dropped and all four ADR-0022 shapes supported, without redesigning anything.

## Wallet

Obsign stops offering the two Custos-hosted `did:web` shapes, with the reason stated on the screen rather than the options quietly vanishing. The `DidWebHosting` type, the `hosting` props, and the `enable_managed_hosting` IPC plumbing all stay — hiding shapes in a client is a sensible default but never the boundary — so lifting the deferral is a UI change.

## Verification

- `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude identity-wallet --exclude admin-companion --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test` (Linux-lane scope) — **2666 passed, 0 failed**
- New coverage: 7 unit tests on the `#device` predicate (`#atproto` is never authority; duplicate entries fail closed; each predicate field enforced; multibase rendering) and 2 route tests (a Custos-hosted `did:web` is refused before any outbound resolution and spends no nonce; an unsupported DID method shares the same opaque rejection)
- `pnpm check` — 434 files, 0 errors · `pnpm test` — 158 passed
- Non-compile gates: fmt, lock-check, bruno-check, docs-check, changelog-check, changelog-test, ticket-ref-check, auth-seam-check, capability-docs-check, ssrf-client-check, runbook-parity-check — all pass
- Screen verified in the browser harness (mobile viewport, no console errors, routing intact)

## Notes for review

- The `did:web` happy path has no route-level test: `did_web_document_url` hardcodes `https://` and rejects IP literals and `localhost`, so a wiremock server is unreachable by construction. The policy is unit-tested on the extractor instead, and the security-critical hosting-gate branch — which returns before any fetch — is covered at the route level.
- ADR-0022 carries an amendment recording the `#device`-only policy, the hosting gate and why it is exact, and the deferral.
- Interim operational note from the issue: keep a password set on `did:web:malpercio.dev` until this deploys, purely as a second key to the door.

The 18-line file was cleanly **deleted** (it was exactly 18 lines), with no dangling importers — not dead code. Review complete.

## Review: PR #442 (merged) — did:web sovereign sessions + wallet-confirmed OAuth consent (MM-475)

### Verdict

**Faithful to every decision we specified, and the security-critical properties all held up under inspection.** This is the right shape: one new module, two routes losing their duplicated gate, policy enforced server-side, UI deferral honest about why.

### Properties verified against the merged code

- **Ordering preserved on both routes.** Sovereign: syntax → freshness → *local-account gate* → signature → authority. Consent: pending-row binding → signature → authority. An unsigned or invalid probe still triggers no outbound fetch on either path.
- **Hosting gate fires before any network I/O**, and the route test proves it the strong way — the mock PLC mounts nothing and `plc.verify()` passes, plus the nonce is asserted unspent. Gate polarity correct (`enabled → refused`).
- **Predicate parity with `create_did.rs`** — `type`/`controller`/exact-id all enforced, each covered by a unit test, including the two cases I most wanted: `#atproto` is never authority, and duplicate `#device` entries fail closed rather than resolving by array order.
- **Opaque-rejection posture intact.** `Unauthorized` collapses into the routes' existing single messages; `Lookup` propagates with its own status — the same deliberate fail-closed-with-status posture the PLC path always had, now documented on the enum.
- **Cache untouchable.** Both arms resolve live, with the why-per-method comment (`rotationKeys` authority semantics; the cache is writable by `/v1/did-web/document`).
- **The malformed-DID fallthrough is safe**: `did:plc:tooshort` fails `is_plc_did`, doesn't match `did:web:`, lands in `unsupported_did_method` — it can never drift into the web arm.
- **Wallet**: 4 shapes → 2, deferral stated on-screen with a reason ("We would rather offer nothing than offer that" — exactly the honest-never-hype register), `didWebHosting` frozen to `'self'` with the un-deferral path documented in a comment, plumbing retained. ADR-0022 amendment records the policy, the gate's exactness, and the deferral, matching what we decided verbatim.

### Findings (follow-ups, nothing blocking)

1. **`crates/pds/AGENTS.md` is now stale** — the one gap. The routes table still describes `sovereign_session.rs` as "signed by a key in the hosted DID's authoritative current PLC `rotationKeys`," the `oauth_consent` module comment's counterpart in the table likewise, and the `identity/` module table doesn't list `authority.rs` at all. Nothing gates this (docs-check covers generated pages, not AGENTS.md), so it'll silently mislead the next session that loads it. Small PR or fold into the next dream-routine pass.
2. **Asymmetry worth one sentence somewhere**: the consent route (unlike sovereign, which has the local-account pre-gate) will run `web_authority` for a DID with no local account — the hosting probe finds no row, returns false, and the fetch proceeds. An attacker with a pending consent request and their own keypair can thus induce a fetch of `https://<their-domain>/.well-known/did.json`. Not a new class — `resolveDid` already offers arbitrary did:web resolution unauthenticated, the fetch is SSRF-hardened and rate-limited, and the pre-change PLC path had the same shape (fetch for any claimed DID) — but a local-account pre-check on the approve path would cost one indexed query and remove the asymmetry.
3. The acknowledged test gap (no route-level did:web happy path, since `did_web_document_url` hardcodes `https://`) is reasonable given the unit coverage — but it makes the **live verification the actual happy-path test**, which brings me to:

### The verification that closes this arc

Once this ships in the next release, `did:web:malpercio.dev` is the perfect live subject — your `did.json` already carries `#device`, and we confirmed `did_web_hosting_enabled_at` is NULL. The wallet's "Unlock identity" biometric flow against prod is the end-to-end proof. If it mints a session: MM-475 verified, and **the interim password can come off the account** — at which point every thread from this conversation (the OAuth lockout that started it, the blob incident it uncovered, and the recovery-path dependency that made this urgent) is actually, fully closed.

1. **The most likely failure mode is a key mismatch, and it's silent by design.** Every rejection is the same opaque 401, so if it fails, the *reason* is only in the server log — grep for `approval rejected` / `sovereign session proof rejected`; the WARN line carries `reason`, `account_did`, and `signing_key_did`. If it works, the arc is closed, and the last cleanup is the interim password — one wrinkle there: no route *un-sets* a password (`resetPassword` only ever sets one; the admin repair route deliberately refuses to touch passwordless accounts), so returning to `password_hash = NULL` is a one-line prod SQL when you're ready.

content.text:
Fix verified and cleaned up. Summary:

**What was missed:** [+page.svelte:730](apps/identity-wallet/src/routes/+page.svelte:730) gated the `onsignin` prop — the "Sign in to an app" entry to the entire consent-approval surface (QR scan + typed code) — on `did:plc:`. MM-475 rewired the server and the onboarding screens but never touched this gate on the identity-detail screen, so the flow it unlocked was unreachable for exactly the accounts it unlocked it for. Everything beneath the button was already method-agnostic: the Rust consent commands never inspect the DID method, and `discover_pds` resolves did:web documents (the import flow depends on it).

**The fix:** delete the gate — `onsignin={() => goTo('oauth_consent_approval')}` — plus a changelog fragment. Nothing else needed.

**Verified:**
- `svelte-check`: 434 files, 0 errors · unit tests: 158/158
- Browser harness (`rekey-mixed` scenario): the did:web identity now shows **Sign in to an app**, and tapping it loads the consent screen with both the QR-scan and typed-code paths, zero console errors — screenshot above
- Regression direction: the did:plc identity keeps the button *and* all its plc-only actions (Change handle, Repair hosting endpoint, Rotate signing key) — untouched

One deliberate judgment call to flag: the button now renders for **every** identity, including a hypothetical Custos-hosted did:web, which the server would refuse with its opaque 401 at approval time. That's consistent with the merged design ("hiding shapes in a client is a sensible default but never the boundary" — the server gate is the enforcement), and the wallet can't currently create hosted did:webs anyway. If you'd rather the wallet pre-hide it for hosted ones, that needs a capability/hosting probe and I'd call it not worth it now.

The change is sitting on branch `mm-475-didweb-signin-entry` (from fresh `origin/main`), working tree otherwise clean. Want me to commit, push, and open the PR? Once it's deployed — or honestly, once you rebuild the app locally with this one-liner — your OAuth attempt is unblocked.

Follow-up to #442 ([MM-475](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-475/didweb-sovereign-sessions-and-wallet-confirmed-oauth-consent)).

## The miss

#442 made the server's authority lookup method-agnostic and updated the onboarding screens, but the identity detail screen still gated `onsignin` on `did:plc:` — so the **"Sign in to an app"** entry (the whole wallet-confirmed OAuth consent surface: QR scan and typed code alike) never rendered for exactly the did:web accounts the server change unlocked. Found live: a passwordless did:web account had no way to reach the consent approval it was newly entitled to.

Everything beneath the button was already method-agnostic — the consent IPC commands (`preview_oauth_consent*`, `confirm_oauth_consent`) never inspect the DID method, and `discover_pds` resolves did:web documents (the import flow depends on it). The fix is deleting the gate:

```svelte
onsignin={() => goTo('oauth_consent_approval')}
```

## Judgment call

The entry now renders for **every** identity, including a hypothetical Custos-hosted did:web, which the server refuses with its uniform opaque rejection at approval time. That is the boundary by design (#442: "hiding shapes in a client is a sensible default but never the boundary"), and the wallet cannot create hosted did:webs while the deferral stands. Pre-hiding it would need a hosting probe for a case that cannot currently arise.

## Verification

- `pnpm check` — 434 files, 0 errors
- `pnpm test` — 158/158
- Browser harness (`rekey-mixed`, mobile viewport, no console errors): the did:web identity shows "Sign in to an app" and tapping it loads the consent screen with both the QR-scan and typed-code paths; the did:plc identity keeps the entry and all of its plc-only actions (Change handle, Repair hosting endpoint, Rotate signing key) unchanged
- Changelog fragment included

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
